localFacts.fact: idealista's help centre advises shooting rooms in horizontal format and keeping the camera straight (ángulo recto) for vertical lines; the tripod is the ally when light is low.
IACrea's real estate photo guide puts the camera between 1 m and 1,30 m from the floor and says a tripod keeps the same shooting height from room to room.
Spanish terms: rótula de cremallera / rótula de engranajes (geared head), rótula de 3 vías, rótula de bola, zapata / placa de liberación rápida, escuadra en L; Arca-Swiss keeps its name.

localPainPoints.pain: Working out the real camera height: the head and camera add height on top of the legs.
localPainPoints.fix: Use the head heights in the table (11-16 cm); interiors only need 1-1,30 m (IACrea).

quotes.text: cuenta la altura de la rótula unos 10cm y otros 8-10 de la cámara

localGain.point: idealista's own advice (straight camera for vertical lines) linked to the geared head's per-axis control.
IACrea's 1-1,30 m camera height and the head heights in the table.
